title: Fukuoka
dek: Five days in Kyushu for a party of eight — yatai crawls, Hakata ramen, Dazaifu's shrine, and a coastal day trip to Itoshima. Balanced pace, public transit where it's practical.
verified: ⚠ Checked 2026-08-29 for the Oct 19–23, 2026 trip — Pass A (canonical), Pass B (local/authentic, native-Japanese research), and reconciliation are all complete. Entry rules, the transit backbone (Fukuoka Airport↔city, Dazaifu, Itoshima), Dazaifu Tenmangu, Kyushu National Museum, Itoshima's coast, central Fukuoka sights, yatai etiquette (including the Nakasu-vs-Tenjin/Nagahama crowd-and-price distinction, and an indoor group-yatai option for the full party), and Hakata's regional specialties (ramen, motsunabe, mentaiko, udon — including a group-discounted motsunabe course for 8+) are checked against official/primary and, for crowd/authenticity claims, corroborating firsthand sources. One reconciled conflict: Ichiran stays shipped for its founding-shop value, with a note that locals more often eat elsewhere (Shin-Shin named, not independently address/hours-verified). ⚠ re-check before travel: the Nishitetsu Tenjin–Dazaifu fare (Nishitetsu raised fares system-wide Apr 1, 2026; the current figure is only an unconfirmed ≈¥480 aggregator estimate), Nishitetsu and JR Kyushu exact train times (both lines revised their timetables in Mar 2026), Showa Bus Itoshima frequencies and fares (published only as unreadable PDFs this pass), the US State Department advisory level for Japan (travel.state.gov blocks automated access), Nokonoshima Island Park's admission price (aggregator-sourced only), Hakata Okunchi's exact 2026 program (inferred from the fixed Oct 23–24 annual date pattern — not yet posted for 2026), Hakata Yatai Yokocho Kizuimaru's operating status (an aggregator's unconfirmed March 2026 renovation-closure note vs. the operator's own current-looking site — call ahead), and Motsunabe Kobayashi's deposit/cancellation terms (not stated on the operator's site — confirm at booking).
footer: Transit fares, hours, and admission figures are sourced from official operators and city/prefecture tourism sites — tap any citation for the source page.
